literature_notes: Both ledger lines (L1, L2) describe synthetic chimeric constructs (C_VHH LIFRΔ1–8, C_VHH LIFRΔ1–4, C_VHH LIFRΔ1–3, C_VHH EpoRΔD1-LIFR) in which the native extracellular domains of LIFR are deleted and replaced by VHH nanobodies; a Myc tag is present somewhere on these chimeras and is used for flow-cytometric surface detection. These constructs fail on two independent grounds: (1) they are not tag insertions into native, full-length, membrane-anchored LIFR — the entire extracellular portion of the canonical protein is absent — so they cannot ground a site in the canonical sequence; and (2) the position of the Myc tag within the chimeric construct is never stated in either clip, making it impossible to pin insert_after_residue. The 'topology_derived' escape applies only when exactly one extracellular terminus exists in the tagged construct of the target protein; here the extracellular portion is a foreign VHH domain, not LIFR sequence, so no LIFR junction can be derived. No other modality (fluorescent-protein fusion, transposon screen, bungarotoxin-binding site, AviTag, etc.) appears in the ledger. The correct answer is zero qualifying sites.
